top_news.title: Validating the Comparison, Not Just the Scorer: Why Overall Accuracy Can Mislead in Interactive LLM Evaluation
top_news.dek: Researchers warn that relying on overall accuracy metrics for LLM evaluators can mask prompt-specific errors.
top_news.brief: When evaluating LLM responses to varying conversational pressures, researchers often use automatic scorers validated by a single F1 or accuracy score. This study demonstrates that high aggregate performance can hide significant bias, where a scorer performs worse on specific prompt types, leading to skewed measurements of model behavior.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing how aggregate metrics can obscure performance variance across different prompt types.

top_news.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
top_news.dek: Cloudflare's Auto Router uses a classifier to dynamically select models based on request complexity and stakes.
top_news.brief: Cloudflare launched a public beta of Auto Router via AI Gateway. The system classifies incoming requests by complexity, ambiguity, and stakes to route them to the most appropriate model. While Cloudflare claims high success rates at a fraction of the cost of top-tier models, questions remain regarding how the system maintains context and stakes over long agent sessions.
top_news.image_alt: Conceptual flow of Cloudflare AI Gateway routing requests to different LLM endpoints.

top_news.title: PaperPilot – Zero-Cloud, Pure-Rust PDF Engine with WASM and MCP
top_news.dek: PaperPilot is a local, Rust-based PDF processing engine leveraging WASM and MCP.
top_news.brief: PaperPilot provides a zero-cloud document processing solution. By utilizing Rust and WebAssembly, it enables local AI-assisted document interaction, integrating with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to facilitate tool use without external data dependencies.
top_news.image_alt: Architecture diagram of a local PDF processing engine using Rust and WASM.

top_news.title: ManyAgents
top_news.dek: ManyAgents enables users to manage a team of AI coding agents from a single macOS interface.
top_news.brief: ManyAgents is a desktop application designed to orchestrate multiple AI coding agents simultaneously. It provides a centralized dashboard for developers to manage agent workflows and code generation tasks directly from their local machine.
top_news.image_alt: Screenshot of the ManyAgents macOS interface showing multiple active coding agents.

primary.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
primary.summary: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. primary.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
primary.summary: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0
